candidate_text: Codex fixed a subtle unified-exec sandbox bug: approved `require_escalated` / exec-policy bypass decisions now survive zsh-fork launch and intercepted execs, while `with_additional_permissions` stays sandboxed. PR: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/24981
evidence_notes: The upstream review records separate behavior for `UseDefault`, `RequireEscalated`, and `WithAdditionalPermissions`.
PR #24981 says zsh-fork launch work could happen before intercepted child execs and lose approved sandbox decisions.
Unified exec now derives launch sandbox permissions before managed-network, env, and launch sandbox selection.
New tests cover parent approval preservation, policy bypass, bounded additional permissions, denied-read preservation, and proxy env stripping.

claims.text: Approved unified-exec escalation decisions now survive zsh-fork launch and intercepted exec paths.
`with_additional_permissions` remains a bounded sandbox expansion rather than a full unsandboxed override.

decision.reason: The PR changes operator-relevant sandbox and approval semantics with strong source and test evidence.

caveats: Do not imply broader permission expansion beyond approved or policy-allowed cases.
No new CLI flag is introduced by this PR.
next_steps: Let Publisher automation decide whether to reserve or post this after repository checks pass.
